correctness.rationale: The rectangular rook graph is the line graph of its selected row-column bipartite incidence graph; domination is equivalent to no simultaneously isolated row and column. Perfect matchability is equivalent to even edge counts in each nontrivial connected component (proved by pairing incident edges through spanning-tree parity). Exponential formula parity filtering yields exactly the displayed sqrt(A(z)A(-z)) coefficient, and the minimum formulas follow from occupancy. Small board direct enumeration corroborates the stated examples; this is a correct proof, regardless of originality.
